scope.flow: HypoVault performance-fee accounting on share transfer and withdrawal
scope.environment: HypoVault contract with Average Cost Basis accounting and ERC20 transferable shares

statements.text: Alice holds a highly profitable position where market value exceeds her basis.
Bob holds a position at a loss with a high-cost basis.
Bob transfers his shares to Alice, triggering _transferBasis.
_transferBasis adds the incoming basis to the recipient's existing basis without distinguishing the recipient's pre-existing profitable position from the incoming position's financial history.
The merged basis produces an artificially inflated average cost basis in Alice's account that can be made equal to or greater than the current market value of the shares.
The calculated profit becomes zero or negative upon withdrawal, completely eliminating the performance fee.
Any two or more colluding users can systematically and completely evade performance fees, and if widely adopted this would reduce protocol fee income to near zero.
A secondary market for loss trading is created in which users with losing positions sell their high-cost basis to profitable users.
Performance fees should be charged on profitable withdrawals based on each position's own cost basis, and merging a transferred loss basis into a profitable position should not reduce the fee owed.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether Alice and Bob are distinct addresses or whether the transfer is permissionless; collusion is described but no caller authorization is specified.
The fee-elimination outcome is described as manipulable/can be, not as an observed executed transaction.
Unfairness to regular holders and flawed economic model are claimed effects beyond the four extracted impacts.
